anchor.statement: Lemma A.2. Let K = [−1, 1] and suppose a finite family of correction coefficients c ∈ Rm changes the required moments, after taking specified linear combinations of the moments and dividing each resulting component by a specified nonzero factor, by F η (c) = B( η )c + Q η (c, c), η ∈ K. (A.2) Here B and the bilinear map Q are smooth, and B is invertible on K, and the prescribed moment discrepancy is d ∈ C ∞ (K; Rm ). Write β 0 = sup K ∥B −1 ∥, κ 0 = sup K ∥Q∥, and d 0 = ∥d∥ C0(K) . If 8 β 2 0 κ 0 d 0 ≤ 1, there is a unique solution of F η (c) = d( η ) in the ball ∥c∥ C0 ≤ 2 β 0 d 0 . It is smooth in η and is selected by iteration from zero of c ↦→ B( η ) −1 (d( η ) − Q η (c, c)). If Q = 0, there is no smallness requirement. For any preselected finite k, let β k be the operator norm of multiplication by B −1 on C k (K), and let κ k be the corresponding bilinear norm of Q. If also 8 β 2 k κ k ∥d∥ Ck ≤ 1, the same branch satisfies ∥c∥ Ck ≤ 2 β k ∥d∥ Ck . (A.3)

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: Under 8β0²κ0d0 ≤ 1 it gives a smooth solution with ‖c‖_{C0} ≤ 2β0d0, uniqueness among continuous solutions in that ball, convergence of the iteration from zero, and ‖c‖_{Ck} ≤ 2βk‖d‖_{Ck} whenever 8βk²κk‖d‖_{Ck} ≤ 1; with Q = 0 the smallness condition holds automatically.
